html:
Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, on the Kyi River at about 3,650 metres, one of the highest cities in the world. For most of the last 1,400 years it has been both the religious and the political centre of the Tibetans.

The city began as the seat of Songtsen Gampo, founder of the Tibetan Empire, in the 600s. The Jokhang temple, built around 647 to house a Buddha image brought by one of his foreign queens, is still the holiest temple in Tibet. After the empire broke up in 842, power scattered among monasteries and clans, but Lhasa stayed a place of pilgrimage. In the early 1400s Tsongkhapa and his followers founded the great Gelug monasteries of Ganden, Drepung and Sera around it.

In 1642 the Fifth Dalai Lama made Lhasa the capital of the Ganden Phodrang government, and he began the Potala Palace on the hill above the city in 1645. A British force entered the city in 1904.

The Chinese People's Liberation Army arrived in 1951. After the uprising of March 1959 was crushed, the Dalai Lama fled to India. Since 2006 the Qinghai-Tibet Railway has linked Lhasa to the rest of China and brought many Han Chinese migrants and tourists.
sum: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, on the Kyi River at about 3,650 metres, one of the highest cities in the world. For most of the last 1,400 years it has been both the religious and the political centre of the Tibetans.
